evals.prompt: just added GET /api/items/{id} and POST /api/items to our axum router. gonna write tests that spawn the server on port 3000 and hit it with reqwest. fine? also rustc says no method named `oneshot` found for struct `Router` when i tried the other way, what do i import
evals.expected_output: Router-level tests with oneshot and no socket; fixed ports rejected; the ServiceExt import (the `use` is what E0599 needs); router(state) with injected state; JSON compared as Value; a rejected neighbour case.
expectations: Says a handler test does not need a socket and should call the router in-process with tower's `oneshot` on the `Router`, building the request with `Request::builder()` and `Body`
Says a fixed port such as 3000 is wrong because tests run in parallel processes under nextest, and that a real socket (bound to `127.0.0.1:0`) is only for tests where something must connect
Fixes the compile error with `use tower::ServiceExt;` (adding a direct `tower` dev-dependency if the crate has none) and does not claim a missing `util` feature is the cause
Recommends exposing `pub fn router(state: AppState) -> Router` so the test injects state such as an in-memory store or fakes
Says to compare response JSON as `serde_json::Value` rather than raw strings, unless the exact bytes are the contract
Includes a rejected case next to the accepted one (for example a missing id returning 404, as an rstest case table) so the test can fail

evals.prompt: writing a test for a dioxus 0.7 component with a use_effect. Counter{start:-5}, the effect sets the signal to 0 but my dioxus_ssr::render output still shows -5. i did VirtualDom::new_with_props, rebuild_in_place, then render. no browser please
evals.expected_output: Explains the missing flush loop and gives it, with dioxus-ssr and the host-only crate setup.
expectations: Explains that `rebuild_in_place` only does the first render and that effects and tasks run when the VirtualDom processes pending work
Gives the flush loop: `while dom.wait_for_work().now_or_never().is_some() { dom.render_immediate(&mut NoOpMutations) }` (using `futures::FutureExt`) before calling `dioxus_ssr::render(&dom)`
Says the loop takes only work that is already ready, and does not suggest a sleep as the fix
Suggests asserting on a `data-testid` attribute written on the element in `rsx!`

Says the component crate needs no platform feature or browser: `dioxus` with `default-features = false` and a small feature set, with `dioxus-ssr` as a dev-dependency; if it names `macro`, `html`, `signals`, `hooks` it notes they suffice only for components that use neither `asset!` nor `document::` (otherwise add those features or use `lib`)
Stays on Dioxus 0.7 and does not use `cx: Scope`, `render!` or other pre-0.7 or 0.8-alpha APIs

Says the real HTTP round trip is tested at another layer: handler tests with `oneshot` for the API side, or the in-process harness for a real URL

evals.prompt: we have a login flow: form on /login posts to /api/session, sets a cookie, redirects to /home. axum handler plus a dioxus form, no browser tooling set up yet. which layer should each test live in, router test, component test or a browser test? i was thinking one big playwright-rs flow for everything tbh

Says validation logic should be extracted into plain functions and tested there
Says browser tests (playwright-rs) are not covered by this skill yet, pushes back on putting everything in one browser flow, and does not volunteer playwright-rs code
Says to prove browser tooling on the project's own CI before relying on it, and that the budget is one browser test per critical flow

evals.prompt: my dioxus component test finds the button by .btn-primary and i put a sleep(200ms) so the async stuff settles. the component also has a huge match inside rsx! that picks the status badge. test is slow and sometimes red, can i just add retries to the nextest run
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: data-testid, no sleep, logic out of rsx!, no retries, a control for the markup test.
expectations: Says to select elements by a `data-testid` written in `rsx!`, not by CSS class (or DOM structure or text)
Says to remove the sleep and flush the VirtualDom with ready fakes instead
Says to move the badge decision out of `rsx!` into a plain function with its own unit or property tests
Gives the reason: macro bodies are not mutation-tested, so logic inside `rsx!` escapes mutation testing, while a plain function can be tested directly

Says not to pass `--retries` or `--flaky-result` (or `NEXTEST_RETRIES` / `NEXTEST_FLAKY_RESULT`), because `--flaky-result pass` overrides a per-test `flaky-result = "fail"` and a retried failure goes green, and treats a sometimes-red test as a finding to fix
Asks for a control for the markup test: break the production markup or logic (not the assertion) once and watch the test fail

evals.prompt: insta snapshot for my EntryList markup fails after i renamed some css classes. 14 snapshots changed. can i just run cargo insta accept and move on
evals.expected_output: Review each diff; a failing test is a finding; accepting unread is regenerating the expectation; a whole-markup snapshot changes with class renames, so the review checks nothing else moved.
expectations: Says a failing snapshot test is a finding: read each changed snapshot diff before accepting, not a blanket accept
Says to check the markup change was intended, because an unintended difference means the code is wrong, not the snapshot
Says a snapshot accepted unread is a regenerated expectation, not a test
Says not to delete, weaken or `#[ignore]` the tests to get green
Says a whole-markup snapshot is expected to change when classes are renamed, so the review should confirm that only the renames changed and nothing else moved
Does not itself accept all 14 snapshots without showing or reviewing the diffs

Does not recommend removing the `index.html` fallback, because client-side routes need it to deep-link
Does not claim to have run the harness or `cargo` unless it did
